business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of High-Power DC Ultra-Fast Electric Vehicle Chargers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (unitary national jurisdiction; no separate sub-state company registry or tax regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system: Roman-Dutch common law fused with English company-law heritage, under the supremacy of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996; corporate law is codified in the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (modern, principle-based statute); foreign investment protection is governed domestically by the Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006), Annex 1 on Cooperation on Investment
Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA, 2019) including the Investment Protocol
South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2011, as amended by the 2016 Protocol)
South Africa-United States Double Taxation Agreement (1997, as amended by the 2015 Protocol)
Active DTAA network of 80+ agreements, including South Africa-Germany, South Africa-China, and South Africa-Netherlands DTAAs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 and the Companies Second Amendment Act 17 of 2024 (beneficial-ownership filing obligations in force since 27 December 2024); Companies Regulations, 2011 (Regulations 31 and 32); CIPC Notice 16 of 2024 (semi-automated beneficial-ownership filing in Form CoR 44.1); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FIC Act), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); FIC Guidance Note 6 (Politically Exposed Persons) and FIC Directive 9 (customer due diligence). The South African UBO ownership/control threshold is 5%, deliberately lower than the FATF-recommended 25% baseline.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised certified copy of the passport of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin; underlying passport issued by the national passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where origin state is a member of the 1961 Hague Convention) or South African consular legalisation (for non-member origin states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent authority of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or South African consular legalisation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorising incorporation of the South African (Pty) Ltd and appointing signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, authenticated by a notary public of the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or South African consular legalisation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the proposed initial capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the shareholder, with the bank officer's signature notarised
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or South African consular legalisation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified sworn English translation of any non-English supporting document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Accredited or registered sworn translator of the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation of the translator's signature followed by Hague Apostille or South African consular legalisation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every director, shareholder, and UBO against (i) the South African targeted financial sanctions list published by the Financial Intelligence Centre under section 26A of the FIC Act read with POCDATARA; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (iii) the EU consolidated financial-sanctions list; and (iv) the OFAC SDN list, applied as standard bank practice for USD-denominated SWIFT and trade-finance flows. PEP checks are mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons under FIC Act section 21F; PEP status, relationships, and source of wealth must be recorded before incorporation and disclosed in the Form CoR 44.1 beneficial-ownership return. Screening must be re-run within 24 hours before execution of the incorporation memorandum and again before bank account opening; adverse hits require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and, where relevant, reporting to the FIC under section 29 of the FIC Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) electronic services portal (BizPortal): https://eservice.cipc.co.za (formerly www.bizportal.gov.za); name reservation is filed via Form CoR 9.1.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be rendered in Latin/Roman script, in English or any of the 12 official languages of South Africa; non-Latin script names (Arabic, Mandarin, Cyrillic, etc.) are accepted only through a Latin-alphabet transliteration that CIPC can verify. The name must not be offensive, contravene the Constitution, or mislead the public as to the company's activities (section 11(2)(a)-(c) of the Companies Act). A proprietary limited company must display the suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd' at incorporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Building Society, Mutual Bank, Insurance, Assurance, Long-Term Insurer (requires prior Financial Sector Conduct Authority consent)
Trust, Unit Trust, Fund, Portfolio, Exchange, Stock Exchange, Clearing House (requires prior FSCA or Prudential Authority consent)
Medical Scheme, Hospital, Health Scheme (requires prior Council for Medical Schemes or licensing authority consent)
University, College, Technikon (requires prior Department of Higher Education and Training consent)
Co-Operative, Co-Op (requires prior trade-and-industry co-operatives consent)
Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Industries, Board of Trade (requires prior sector body consent)
South Africa, RSA, National, Government, Provincial, Parliament, Municipality, SARS, CIPC, FIC, Reserve Bank (words falsely implying state patronage are prohibited)
Limited, Incorporated (misuse of corporate-status suffixes by entities not entitled to them is prohibited)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may (1) immediately file a fresh Form CoR 9.1 with a revised name; (2) lodge an administrative appeal or request reconsideration by CIPC within 20 business days of the rejection notice; (3) where rejection is based on a third-party objection or conflicting rights, apply to the Companies Tribunal for a determination under section 160 of the Companies Act within the prescribed period; (4) file a judicial review in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. A reserved name may be extended once for a further 180 days upon payment of the statutory extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to a genuine physical South African street address (a post box is unlawful) capable of receiving service of process, with CIPC notified as registered office under section 23 of the Companies Act; serviced-office and virtual-office arrangements of that nature are accepted by CIPC and banks. A wholly non-physical address is non-compliant; for a manufacturing entity, the factory or plant address must be separately recorded as the place of business, and offshore central management could create tax-residence exposure for the (Pty) Ltd.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified estimate: 35-45% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months of operation (CIPC compliance checks, SARS field audits, and NRCS/dtic verification visits to charging-hardware manufacturing sites); near-100% probability of a lender site visit where SWIFT LC or bank trade-finance facilities are used.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 13, 14, 15, 19, 66 and 70, read with the Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1), Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and director consent forms
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow account deposit is required for a (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the authorised share capital is fixed in the MOI and issued shares need not be fully paid at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers listed in the Notice of Incorporation acquire the founding ordinary shares on the terms of the Memorandum of Incorporation, and that the Company commence with the issued share capital stated in the MOI. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be [physical address], South Africa, and that this address and the relevant officer appointments be filed with CIPC. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director, and [Name] as the first accounting officer authorised to maintain financial records and file statutory returns. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors are authorised to open corporate bank accounts and execute all ancillary documents to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search and preparation of governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal (www.cipc.co.za) or an accredited incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed company name on the CIPC company name database to confirm it is not identical, confusingly similar or offensive. Reserve a distinguishable name where required, or proceed with a registration-number-format company name. Draft the MOI with the share structure, director powers and proposed registered office details.
required_dossiers: Certified or electronically verified ID/passport copies of all incorporators and directors
Proposed Memorandum of Incorporation
Name reservation reference, if applicable
Consent to serve as director from each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a reconsideration or choose an alternative name; the company may nevertheless be incorporated under its registration number pending final name approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators prior to filing with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure each incorporator signs the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 15.1) and the MOI. Obtain signed consents from proposed directors. Verify subscriber share allocations, share classes, director details and the physical registered office address. Scan the signed documents for upload. South African signatories may execute by facsimile or electronic signature where permitted; foreign documents must be apostilled if relying on foreign powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Signed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Signed consent to act as director for each director
Record of registered office physical and postal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC identifies unsigned or inconsistent documents, re-execute the affected page and resubmit the corrected PDF before the filing deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation application and pay official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services online transaction portal; CIPC branch at the dtic Campus, Tshwane
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create or access a CIPC e-Services account, select company registration, upload the signed CoR 15.1, MOI and director consents, complete director and shareholder particulars, select private company as the entity type, and pay the prescribed filing fee by card or electronic funds transfer. Retain the acknowledgment of filing and proof of payment.
required_dossiers: Signed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Signed director consents
Proof of payment or fee remittance
Name reservation number, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC will issue an electronic query; respond with corrected documents within the stated query period. If the query period lapses, resubmit the application and pay the applicable fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and company registration particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor application status in CIPC e-Services, download the Certificate of Incorporation and company registration particulars, verify the registration number, incorporation date, company name, directors and registered office, and use these documents for SARS registration, banking and premises licensing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Company registration particulars report
Filed copy of the Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company registration particulars contain errors, apply to CIPC for correction with a supporting affidavit and the relevant CIPC form; obtain an amended registration report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with SARS, UIF and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour (UIF and Compensation Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax and obtain a tax reference number; register for PAYE, UIF and SDL once employees are appointed; register for VAT where taxable supplies reach or are expected to reach the mandatory threshold; register for occupational injury and disease cover under COIDA at the Compensation Fund.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and CIPC company report
Identity documents of directors and beneficial owners
Physical business address and contact details
SARS Business Registration application completed on eFiling
UIF and COIDA registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, correct the declared business activities and supporting information and resubmit; SARS will issue the relevant reference numbers once the registration is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene first board meeting, issue shares and open corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors and corporate banking department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass a written resolution to ratify incorporation, issue subscriber shares, approve share certificates, confirm the registered office, appoint the accounting officer where required, and approve the bank mandate with authorised signatories.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or minutes
Share certificates and share register
Register of directors
Bank mandate and account opening forms
Certificate of Incorporation and CIPC company report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or a counterparty questions board authority, provide certified extracts of the board minutes and the CIPC registration record; the board may ratify by written resolution if a formality is missing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal zoning, building, fire and environmental screening for the industrial premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality building control and fire authority; Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) where environmental authorisation thresholds are triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a zoning certificate or land-use approval for light-industrial manufacturing of EV chargers, submit building plans for municipal approval, secure a fire compliance certificate from the municipal fire and rescue service, and complete an EIA screening report under the 2014 EIA Regulations to determine whether Basic Assessment is required.
required_dossiers: Zoning certificate or land-use approval
Approved building plans and Certificate of Occupancy
Fire certificate from municipal fire and rescue
EIA screening report; Basic Assessment report if triggered
Electrical installation Certificate of Compliance (CoC)
COIDA registration certificate, once employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or fire authority refuses approval, rectify the noted building or fire safety defects and resubmit; if a Basic Assessment is required, follow the NEMA public participation and appeal process before commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NRCS compulsory specification compliance and manufacturing authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS), Electrical and Electronics Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the DC fast EV charging station is covered by an electrical compulsory specification, submit the product technical file and test reports from a SANAS-accredited laboratory or IECEE-recognised body, and obtain the NRCS Letter of Authority or permit to manufacture and place the product on the South African market.
required_dossiers: NRCS application form
Test reports and CB Test Certificate showing compliance with IEC 61851-1 and IEC 61851-23, as applicable
Technical design file and schematics
ISO 9001 quality management certificate, if applicable
Electrician Certificate of Compliance for the factory installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a non-conformity is raised, submit a corrective action plan, re-test with an accredited laboratory or upgrade components, and apply to the NRCS for reconsideration; judicial review in the High Court remains available for a final refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS); Department of Employment and Labour for workplace safety; local municipality for building and fire approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Letter of Authority / Compulsory Specification Compliance Certificate for electrical EV charging equipment, together with municipal Certificate of Occupancy; no financial or banking licence is required for hardware manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and the relevant provincial environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening / Basic Assessment category under the EIA Regulations, 2014; full Scoping and EIA is not expected for a conventional EV charger assembly plant unless sensitive environmental features or high-risk hazardous waste activities are triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge requires a water use licence or permit under the National Water Act 36 of 1998; volatile organic compounds, particulates and noise must comply with the Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 and municipal by-laws; hazardous waste storage and disposal must comply with the Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire certificate issued by municipal fire and rescue after compliance with the National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977; structural load inspection by a registered professional engineer; Certificate of Occupancy for industrial premises; electrical Certificate of Compliance; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; COIDA registration with the Compensation Fund.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); online portal: SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a South African income tax reference number and VAT number by registering as a taxpayer through SARS eFiling or a branch office. The registration procedure involves: (i) applying for an income tax number using the SARS Registration Form (RAF01) or via eFiling under 'Register a Taxpayer'; (ii) submitting certified copies of the foreign company's incorporation documents, a valid South African branch registration (where applicable), and the directors' or public officer's identification; (iii) registering for VAT using VAT101 if taxable supplies exceed R1 million or voluntarily if above R50,000; and (iv) obtaining a Customs Code through the SARS Customs system for export/import activity. Foreign companies may appoint a local representative taxpayer or tax practitioner to manage the process electronically through eFiling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not offer a US-style check-the-box election. Election mechanisms relevant to a proprietary limited company include: (i) Small Business Corporation (SBC) election under section 12E of the Income Tax Act for qualifying shareholders; (ii) group tax registration for VAT under section 50(3) of the VAT Act for multiple companies in a group; (iii) the election of a micro business tax regime under the Sixth Schedule for turnover not exceeding R1 million; (iv) the hybrid mismatch election rules under sections 8E, 8EA and 23K which allow alignment of tax treatment with the counterpart jurisdiction; and (v) the 'considered acquired' capital gain election for intra-group asset transfers under paragraph 65 of the Eighth Schedule.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 in taxable supplies during any 12-month period (compulsory registration); voluntary registration permitted from R50,000 per year. A foreign entity supplying imported or locally delivered EV charging hardware must register for VAT from the date when taxable supplies exceed the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance electronic invoicing system as of the current regime. SARS requires tax invoices meeting the conditions of section 20 of the VAT Act, issued within 21 days of the supply. SARS is progressively introducing a mandatory e-invoicing interoperability model via the eFiling platform, with API-based submissions for Value-Added Tax returns (VAT201) and customs declarations. No digital stamping of invoices is currently imposed; however, taxpayers must maintain audit-ready electronic records and use SARS-approved electronic billing systems where invoices are transmitted electronically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A vendor may zero-rate exports of goods under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when the goods are physically removed from South Africa to a destination of another country within 90 days of the supply, and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Zero-rating of services is available under section 11(2)(l) for services supplied to non-residents when the services directly relate to moveable goods located outside South Africa, or are performed outside South Africa. The claimant must be a registered VAT vendor, have received export consideration in foreign currency or via approved payment rails, and maintain evidence that the goods left the Republic.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) accepted by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Air Waybill (for air freight)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer statement proving receipt of export proceeds
Proof of physical removal from the South African customs controlled area
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may scrutinise claims for zero-rated export supplies by verifying the customs declaration and foreign exchange repatriation records. Where export documentation is found to be fraudulent or substantively deficient, the full 15% VAT is reclaimed with interest, and the taxpayer becomes liable to an understatement penalty under the Tax Administration Act ranging from 10% to 50% of the shortfall, plus an additional tax up to 200% in cases of deliberate non-disclosure or intentional tax evasion. Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act may also apply for fraudulent export invoices, and retrospective clawback assessment may be issued within the five-year prescription period, extended indefinitely for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, with delegated authority to Authorised Dealers and Authorised Brokers licensed under the Currency and Exchanges Manual.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a partially convertible currency regime. Current account transactions, including trade settlements, service payments, interest, royalties, and dividends, are freely remittable through an Authorised Dealer upon production of the required supporting documents. Capital account transactions executed by South African residents remain subject to FinSurv approval or Authorised Dealer authorisation, while inward non-resident capital investment is generally permitted without prior Exchange Control approval but must be reported and properly documented. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after compliance with exchange control formalities, South African dividend tax at 20% or lower under a relevant double tax agreement, and beneficial ownership declarations. Practical remittance hurdles include the requirement to obtain a South African Revenue Service tax compliance status, submission of documentary proof of original inward capital transfer for capital repatriations, and the burden of satisfying the receiving bank's risk-based source-of-funds and anti-money laundering review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under South African exchange control regulations, all export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of export shipment and must be credited to a South African bank account or a designated foreign currency account held with an Authorised Dealer. There is no mandatory percentage conversion of export receipts into South African rand; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in an approved foreign currency account or convert it to rand at the prevailing market rate. The exporter must provide the bank with the customs export declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, and evidence of receipt of payment. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory 180-day timeline is a contravention of the Exchange Control Regulations and may result in penalties, adverse customs ratings, and exchange control enforcement action.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.mandatory_conversion_ratio: 0% statutory conversion to ZAR is generally required; full repatriation to a South African Authorised Dealer account is mandatory within 180 days.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited, acting through the First National Bank (FNB) division

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The viability of offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) as a primary treasury and clearing rail is LOW. South Africa does not issue an electronic money institution licence equivalent to the EU EMI passport, and only SARB-licensed banks appointed as Authorised Dealers can lawfully maintain corporate ZAR accounts and process cross-border payments. An offshore EMI may be used solely as a payment-orchestration interface or FX quotation layer, but final settlement must be routed through a South African bank account held by the resident entity. Relying on an unlicensed foreign EMI for corporate cash custody or for executing trade settlements may breach the Financial Sector Regulation Act and the National Payment System Act, and would materially impair audit trail and exchange control compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African financial law under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) requires account-taking institutions to conduct client due diligence and expressly verify beneficial ownership, but it does not prescribe a universal mandatory physical interview. In practice, for a locally incorporated (Pty) Ltd with non-resident shareholders or directors, Tier-1 banks require at least one director, alternate director, or authorised representative to attend an in-person or supervised video KYC interview before account activation. New cross-border accounts without an existing bank relationship generally require physical presence at a branch or at a designated foreign representative office. Where the sole signatory is offshore, the bank may impose additional conditions, including notarised certified copies of passports, apostilled board resolutions, a local resident compliance officer, or a locally resident alternate director. Remote opening is possible only where the bank maintains a dedicated offshore digital onboarding channel and the standard risk assessment permits it.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or opaque beneficial ownership information, particularly the presence of trust or multi-layer corporate ownership structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register; full shareholder register; organisational chart showing natural person UBOs; certified passport copies of all UBOs; notarised trust deed or corporate formation documents; sworn declaration confirming source of control; board resolution appointing authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection without a clear economic nexus, or unusually rapid accumulation of ZAR working capital from a non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising the share issue or shareholder loan; executed share subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement; bank reference from the remitting bank; source-of-funds evidence including audited financial statements, tax returns and bank statements; inward SWIFT MT103 confirmation; SARS tax compliance status of the receiving entity; purpose narrative referencing foreign direct investment in EV charging infrastructure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export or trade payment patterns that are inconsistent with the stated high-power DC charger manufacturing business, including mismatched counterparties or third-party settlement instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated purchase orders and proforma invoices; bills of lading, airway bills and Cargo Exit manifest documents; SAD500 customs export declarations; transport and warehousing receipts; independent inspection or quality certificates; full invoice-to-settlement reconciliation trail linking trade flows to treasury outflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or signatories with limited South African footprint and no local tax or address history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passport copies of all directors; original certificate of incorporation and directors' register; proof of residential address in the home jurisdiction; cross-border banker's or professional reference confirming identity; FATCA and CRS self-certification forms; certified board resolution listing mandated signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure, politically exposed persons (PEPs), or perceived concentration risk arising from foreign shareholder jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP and sanctions screening questionnaire; negative sanctions screening report from the onboarding bank; source-of-wealth statement supported by independent evidence; professional reference from an attorney or chartered accountant; purpose and expected transaction profile for the ZA_PTY_LTD entity; consent to enhanced continuous monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed by SWIFT MT103 with clear sender-to-recipient information identifying the transfer as equity subscription or shareholder loan funding for ZA_PTY_LTD. The remitting bank must include a valid payment purpose code corresponding to inward Foreign Direct Investment or intercompany financing. The South African beneficiary bank will verify the underlying board resolution, the executed share subscription or loan agreement, the company certificate of incorporation, the CIPC beneficial ownership filing and the FATCA/CRS self-certification before crediting the ZAR operational account or designated capital escrow account. The bank must record the inward transfer for exchange control and balance-of-payment purposes. Remitters should not use general remittance narratives such as 'family support' or 'consulting fees', as those create an unrebuttable mismatch with the manufacturing business scope and may trigger extended AML review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlements with foreign suppliers and trade counterparties, SWIFT MT103 is the suitable clearing rail for open-account transactions, especially for component imports and recurring raw material payments. For high-value equipment purchases or to secure supply terms, a Commercial Letter of Credit transmitted via SWIFT MT700 and issued subject to UCP 600 provides bank-mediated settlement with preferred payment security; MT707 is used for amendments and MT760 for standby letters of credit or bank guarantees. Each outbound disbursement must be supported by the commercial invoice, proof of goods receipt or services rendered, relevant customs declarations, and an exchange-control underlying-transaction declaration completed through the authorised dealer. Cross-border payments should be made directly to the beneficial trade counterparty and not to unpoliced third-party collection accounts unless the bank has approved a documented special purpose arrangement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FX forwards) with a licensed South African Authorised Dealer to hedge committed current or capital account exposures
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency debt facilities, subject to FinSurv or authorised-dealer approval and genuine underlying exposure
Purchased foreign currency options to hedge confirmed procurement, export revenue, or foreign-currency debt obligations

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where expressly allowed by FinSurv or approved by an Authorised Dealer as an exceptional hedge for a genuine underlying transaction; speculative NDFs are not permissible onshore
Interest rate swaps and forward rate agreements associated with qualifying foreign-currency debt, when used to reduce financing risk rather than create leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CoR 36.1) incorporating annual beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of company registration; filing window opens on the first day of the anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty applies from day 31 after the anniversary per the CIPC penalty schedule; continued default beyond 60 business days after a CIPC notice exposes the company to administrative deregistration/strike-off under s.82 read with s.26 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, with possible director liability for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) prepared within six months of financial year-end, audited or independently reviewed, and filed with CIPC if the public interest score is 350 or more or otherwise prescribed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC for filing; Board and Shareholders for adoption; registered independent auditor or registered accountant for reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's financial year-end (Companies Act s.30(4)); CIPC filing aligned with the annual return cycle where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or table AFS is an offence under s.30 read with s.214; CIPC may issue a compliance notice; persistent non-compliance may lead to enforcement referral, administrative strike-off, and personal liability of directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies when the public interest score (PIS) equals or exceeds 350 points. For PIS between 100 and 349, an audit is compulsory only if required by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights, the CIPC, or a regulatory authority; otherwise an independent review by a registered accountant is sufficient. For PIS below 100, an independent review is the default unless shareholders require a full audit. PIS is calculated as the number of employees plus one point per R1 million of third-party liabilities plus the number of shareholders plus the number of directors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for companies subject to a compulsory audit; IFRS for SMEs permitted for eligible small- and medium-sized private companies (South African GAAP follows IFRS for SMEs).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The (Pty) Ltd must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and submit it to CIPC. The annual return contains an obligatory annual confirmation that the register is accurate and current. Any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers, must be lodged with CIPC within 30 days of the change; failure to comply is a criminal offence under s.56 read with s.213 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150 – $450 (registered office facility and outsourced company secretarial / annual return administration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000 – $6,000 per statutory audit; $800 – $1,600 for an independent review where audit is not compulsory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment commencing on/after 1 April 2022; proposed reduction to 26% per 2025 Budget, effective for years ending on/after 31 March 2026, subject to enactment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 12C: 40/20/20/20 accelerated wear-and-tear for manufacturing plant; Section 12B: 125% first-year deduction for renewable-energy assets; Section 12U: R0.95/kWh energy-efficiency-savings incentive; 2025 Budget proposal: 125% deduction for EV charging infrastructure (pending enactment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carry-forward (no statutory time limit), subject to Section 20A forfeiture where >50% change in shareholding and trade not continued for dominant profit purposes
